newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges softer, cargoes talked higher.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges softer, cargoes talked higher.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges eased on Wednesday with low bunker demand sapping the market, while cargoes were talked higher but buyer caution continued, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded three times at $85 a tonne fob in the ARA area after earlier deals at $86 and $86.25, compared with deals on Tuesday ranging between a low of $85.50 and a high of $87.
Later, two traders were heard offering to sell at $85 a tonne fob Rotterdam after talk was stuck in the $86/$86.50 range in the morning.
"Bunker demand is not very good," one trader said, putting it at about 12,000 tonnes for the day. Others seconded that view, quoting similar numbers.
But traders were mixed about supply, with some saying there was no shortage of avails and others saying that the absence of Russian material means supplies were thinner.
No deals were reported on the high sulphur cargo market but traders said higher numbers were being asked but no serious bids were coming in.
Buyers said that that Monday's high trade at $81.75 fob Coryton, although dismissed by many as not reflecting the market, was still keeping some at bay as sellers upped their prices.
One trader was offering a cargo at $82 fob and a second one was asking $79 fob.
"I don't think there is that much buying interest," one high sulphur fuel oil buyer said. "I was offered some material but we did not go as far as discussing prices," he added.

A major U.K. electrcity utility said it was not planning to buy any high sulphur for burning in the short term, with an official adding: "In general, burns are very low across Europe as we head into the summer, it's the seasonality."
One percent started to show signs of life, with traders saying that buyers and sellers began talking more actively but were still far apart with bids in the low $90s and offers in the mid $90s.
At least four cargoes were being offered and one 25kt low sulphur cargo was heard traded on Tuesday at a floating price, fob ARA plus a small premium of about $1.
"The market is looking a bit longer. Several people are offering cargoes," one trader said.
"People are talking today but it's all about whether they be fixed or floating prices," a second trader said.
